answer: An agent marketplace allocates shared compute by votes weighted by tokens locked for 30 days, rather than by account count. Agents running an oasis simulator, an orchard planner, or a juniper nursery service follow the same rule. Splitting 100 locked tokens among a thousand fake identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital for the full period.
